newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Leumi results exclude asset sales.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi results exclude asset sales.

text.p: Bank Leumi Ltd said on Monday its 1996 results do not include a 450 million shekel net gain from the sale of non-banking holdings.
This gain will appear in the bank's results for the first quarter of 1997.

The bank's president and CEO Galia Maor told a news conference that excluding a 187.1 million shekel provision for expenses for its voluntary retirement programme, the bank's profit in 1996 was 666.6 million shekels, up 47 percent over 1995.
Israel's second biggest bank in 1996 reduced its number of employees by 389, or 3.0 percent.

Maor attributed the rise in profits mainly to an increase in banking activities as well as to a decline in its doubtful debts provision. Credit to the public in 1996 rose 9.1 percent to 80.0 billion shekels while deposits rose 10.1 percent to 107.4 billion shekels.
Assets of its mutual funds totalled 4.1 billion shekels at the end of 1996 while assets controlled by its provident funds amounted to 21.8 billion shekels.
Its net return on equity in 1996 rose to 8.1 percent, including the retirement programme provision, against 6.9 percent in 1995.
Shareholders' equity rose 5.3 percent to 7.3 billion shekels while total assets grew 7.0 percent to 133.4 billion shekels.
